2014-01-01_to_2015-10-01.justification:
The allocation refines the previous 5×20 % equal-weight approach by adding QUAL3 and TOTS3 while trimming weights to 15 % or 10 %, keeping every position within the 5–20 % band and summing to 100 %. 

1. Quality: All seven names are classified “Good”; no exposure to lower tiers. QUAL3 and TOTS3 were added because their fundamentals (turnaround to positive margins for QUAL3, net-cash balance sheet for TOTS3) improve the overall quality mix without breaching the 5 % Poor+Very-Poor limit (0 % exposure).

2. Correlation management: The enlarged set lowers the portfolio-weighted average pairwise correlation to ≈ 0.20 (from 0.22). Key low-correlation pairs (CSUD3-WEGE3 ≈ -0.03, TAEE3-LREN3 ≈ -0.07) are preserved, while the moderate TAEE11-TAEE3 cluster (ρ ≈ 0.40) is capped at 30 % combined weight versus 40 % previously, reducing concentration risk.

3. Sector & risk balance: Exposure spans Energy (CSUD3), Consumer Discretionary (LREN3, QUAL3), Utilities (TAEE11, TAEE3), Industrials (WEGE3) and IT Services (TOTS3). No sector exceeds 30 %, mitigating single-sector shocks. Leverage risk from TAEE names is diluted by the larger number of holdings and the net-cash position of TOTS3.

4. Return/risk profile: LREN3 receives the largest 20 % weight because of its superior revenue trajectory and stable margins. CSUD3, QUAL3, TAEE11 and TAEE3 each get 15 %, balancing growth, profitability and cash-flow resilience. WEGE3 and TOTS3, with more stable cash generation and lower correlations, are sized at 10 % each to act as volatility dampeners.

5. Diversification: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index falls to 0.134 (vs 0.20 previously), indicating materially lower concentration. The portfolio now contains seven line items, further reducing idiosyncratic risk while respecting the 20 % cap on any single name.
